---

# SEC Filing Analysis: Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S — 8-K / June 25, 2026

---

## A. Relevance Verdict

**RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a direct private-credit fund disclosure. It reports portfolio composition, new loan activity, NAV, and a new share issuance from a semi-liquid, non-traded BDC-adjacent vehicle managed by Lord Abbett. The filing is directly on-theme given the current wave of redemption pressure and software-sector scrutiny across the private-credit universe.

---

## B. One-Line Takeaway

Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S discloses a $409M, 95%-senior-secured portfolio with 14.2% combined software/IT exposure, 4.9x leverage, and a steady but modest $3.4M equity raise — no redemption stress, no non-accruals, but operating squarely within the sectors under market-wide scrutiny.

---

## C. What's New

- **New equity issuance disclosed:** ~137,784 common shares sold as of June 1, 2026, at **$24.64/share**, for ~**$3.4 million** in aggregate proceeds under Section 4(a)(2)/Reg D to accredited investors; share count finalized June 22, 2026.
- **Six new portfolio company loan commitments** were added during May 2026 alone, totaling **$39.2 million in commitments** and **$36.8 million in par value**, including first-time named borrowers: **Advanced Integration Technology LP** ($19.5M), **International Aerospace Coatings Holdings LP** ($11.9M committed, $10.8M funded), **PT Intermediate Holdings III, LLC** ($2.0M), and **SCHP Purchaser, Inc.** ($4.5M).
- **Fresh NAV and per-share figure disclosed:** NAV of approximately **$197 million**; NAV/share of **$24.64** as of May 31, 2026. This is the most current public valuation for this fund.
- **New distribution declared:** $0.19/share declared June 23, 2026, to shareholders of record June 30, 2026, payable on or about **July 28, 2026** — the first distribution event disclosed in this filing cycle.
- **Portfolio aggregate loan commitment now at ~$525 million** against par value of ~$409 million — a $116M unfunded commitment overhang disclosed explicitly for the first time in this filing.
- **Industry composition table newly published:** First public breakdown showing **Aerospace & Defense at 16.0%**, **Software at 7.5%**, and **IT Services at 6.7%** — combined tech/software exposure of ~14.2% by par value.

---

## D. Most Important Points

- **Fund size:** NAV ~$197 million; aggregate loan commitments ~$525 million; par value ~$409 million. A mid-small vehicle relative to sector giants but a meaningful unfunded pipeline of ~$116 million (22% of par).
- **Portfolio composition:** 95% senior secured debt, 5% joint venture, 100% floating rate. 99% of commitments in private senior secured loans — clean, conservative structure on paper.
- **Credit metrics as of May 31, 2026:** WA net leverage 4.9x; WA LTV 44%; WA interest coverage **2.4x**; median EBITDA $91 million; WA yield at cost **9.2%**. The 4.9x leverage is moderate vs. the broader market (FSB/UBS cite 5–6x reported, up to 7x adjusted), but the 2.4x interest coverage leaves limited cushion if EBITDA softens.
- **Software + IT Services exposure = ~14.2%** ($30.9M software + $27.4M IT services = $58.3M by par). This is a material concentration given market-wide anxiety over AI disruption risk in software names. Private credit funds are major lenders to software companies, including SaaS firms, with exposures estimated at around $500 billion as of December 2025, and AI-driven revenue disruptions have contributed to redemption waves at funds with sector exposure.
- **Aerospace & Defense = largest single sector at 16.0% ($65.4M)** — a relatively defensive and government-revenue-linked sector; Air Freight & Logistics at 9.7% ($39.8M) is worth watching given macro freight sensitivity.
- **Equity issuance modest:** Only ~$3.4M raised in the latest subscription cycle — suggests slow retail/accredited investor inflow into this particular share class ("S"), consistent with broad BDC fundraising softness. For perpetually non-traded BDCs, inflows shifted to the first-ever outflow in Q1 2026, according to Moody's data.
- **No non-accruals, no PIK, no defaults, no redemption gate disclosed** — the fund appears operationally clean in this filing.
- **All debt investments are floating rate** — borrowers face full pass-through of current rate environment; no fixed-rate insulation.
- **Fund formerly named "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund A, LP"** (name changed October 2024 to "Fund S") — the entity is relatively young and is still building scale.
- **Recurring revenue borrower present:** One investment excluded from weighted-average metrics is a "recurring revenue investment" (i.e., an ARR-based loan, not EBITDA-based) — a structurally riskier loan type that receives no further disclosure in this filing.

---

## E. Why It Matters Now

This filing lands at the epicenter of the 2026 private-credit redemption and software-risk storm. So-called semi-liquid private debt vehicles have been subject to a wave of redemption pressure in 2026, as investors look to pull money amid growing anxieties over asset quality and the mismatch between private assets and the retail wealth channel. Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S shows none of those stress signals directly — no redemption cap breach, no gating, no non-accruals — but its ~14.2% combined software/IT exposure is a live watchpoint given that recent headlines around software exposure, AI disruption, non-accruals, PIK activity, and redemptions in certain vehicles have made some capital providers more selective. The modest $3.4M equity raise is consistent with the broader industry picture where "private credit fund demand began to slow in 2025's second half as concerns over software exposure and lower base rates cooled investors on the asset class." The fund's 2.4x interest coverage ratio is the metric most worth tracking if rates remain elevated or EBITDA weakens — it is tight relative to a stressed scenario.

## SEC Filing Analysis: Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund — 8-K / June 25, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict

**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a registered private credit fund filing its monthly operational update. It discloses portfolio metrics, new loan activity, NAV, distributions, and a small equity issuance — all core private-credit data.

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway

Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund disclosed a ~$727M NAV, $1.46B in loans to 60 companies at 2.4x interest coverage and 4.9x net leverage, with $107.6M in new May commitments and a modest $5.7M equity raise.

---

### C. What's New

- **New equity issuance disclosed:** ~231,222 Common Shares sold at $24.79/share for ~$5.7M aggregate proceeds as of June 1, 2026 (final count determined June 22, 2026) — a notably small raise relative to total portfolio size (~$1.46B par).
- **Six new borrowers named** for loan activity in May 2026: Advanced Integration Technology LP, Ambient Enterprises Holdco LLC, ICAT Intermediate Holdings LLC, International Aerospace Coatings Holdings LP, PT Intermediate Holdings III LLC, and SCHP Purchaser Inc. — most not previously disclosed in this filing context.
- **Two commitments with zero drawn par:** ICAT Intermediate Holdings LLC ($7.9M committed, $0 drawn) and Ambient Enterprises Holdco LLC ($0.3M committed, $0 drawn) — unfunded exposure with no current par value.
- **Monthly distribution declared:** ~$0.22/share declared June 23, 2026; record date June 30, 2026; payable ~July 28, 2026.
- **Point-in-time NAV disclosed:** $727M aggregate / $24.79 per share as of May 31, 2026 — matches the per-share equity issuance price, confirming no markup/markdown at issuance.
- **"Recurring revenue" investment excluded from all portfolio metrics** — one undisclosed borrower whose credit is underwritten on revenue multiples, not EBITDA, is silently carved out of leverage, coverage, and LTV calculations, obscuring true portfolio-wide risk.
- **Former name change noted:** Previously filed as "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund 1, LP"; name changed effective January 18, 2024 — structural evolution of the vehicle worth tracking for peer comparison.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- **Portfolio size:** 60 portfolio companies; $1,933M aggregate loan commitments; $1,463M funded par value — implies ~$470M in undrawn commitments (24% of total commitments unfunded).
- **Floating-rate exposure: 100%** of debt investments by par value are at floating rates — full exposure to rate-cut risk on income compression; yield compression threat as rates decline.
- **Weighted average yield: 9.4%** (at cost) — in line with current market but watch for compression as reference rates fall.
- **Interest coverage: 2.4x** — thin by historical standards; limited cushion against EBITDA deterioration or further rate movement.
- **Net leverage: 4.9x** — moderate-to-elevated for middle-market private credit; combined with 2.4x coverage, signals borrowers are operating close to the edge.
- **LTV: 44%** — relatively conservative; provides structural protection on collateral, but sponsor-estimated enterprise values are used, not independently verified.
- **Software sector exposure: $108.0M (7.4% of par)** — plus IT Services ($132.4M / 9.1%) = combined tech/software exposure of ~16.5% of portfolio, a meaningful concentration.
- **New May commitments: $107.6M** across six issuers — aerospace, industrial coatings, and unnamed sectors (SCHP Purchaser Inc. sector not identified); pace of deployment appears active.
- **95% senior secured / 5% JV** by par — overwhelmingly first-lien senior secured; structurally protective.
- **Emerging growth company status confirmed** — still early in its lifecycle relative to peers; NAV of $727M is below scale of leading BDC peers.

---

### E. Why It Matters Now

The 2.4x weighted-average interest coverage and 4.9x net leverage are the headline risk metrics to watch: they indicate that, on average, borrowers are not comfortably serviced, and a modest EBITDA decline or rate shock could push multiple credits toward stress. The 100% floating-rate portfolio means that any Fed rate cuts will compress income without necessarily relieving borrower stress immediately, as rate reset timing lags. The software and IT services concentration (~16.5% combined) is directly in line with current market concern about tech-borrower underwriting risk. The $5.7M equity raise is strikingly small versus the $1.46B portfolio — fundraising does not appear to be accelerating, which could constrain the fund's ability to fund its ~$470M undrawn commitment pipeline. The filing is otherwise consistent with a normally functioning private credit fund and does not show overt liquidity stress or defaults.

---

### F. Filing Details Extracted

- **Filer:** Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund (CIK 0002008748)
- **Form type:** 8-K
- **Filing date:** June 25, 2026
- **Period of report:** June 22, 2026
- **Company / fund / issuer:** Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund (Delaware; formerly Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund 1, LP)
- **Named lenders / agents / counterparties:** Not disclosed (lender identity not named); borrowers named: Advanced Integration Technology LP, Ambient Enterprises Holdco LLC, ICAT Intermediate Holdings LLC, International Aerospace Coatings Holdings LP, PT Intermediate Holdings III LLC, SCHP Purchaser Inc.
- **Dollar amounts:** NAV ~$727M; par value ~$1,463M; total commitments ~$1,933M; undrawn ~$470M; equity raise ~$5.7M; May new commitments $107.6M / $96.3M drawn; distribution ~$0.22/share
- **Maturity dates:** Not disclosed in this filing
- **Interest-rate / spread terms:** 100% floating rate; weighted average yield at cost 9.4%; reference rate + spread (specific spread not disclosed)
- **Key covenant or amendment terms:** Not disclosed
- **Sector:** Private credit / BDC-equivalent (non-traded); top exposures — Aerospace & Defense (11.7%), Health Care (10.0%), IT Services (9.1%), Electrical Equipment (9.0%), Software (7.4%)
- **Watchlist entity match:** Unknown — no individual credit named as non-accrual, watchlist, or distressed; one "recurring revenue" borrower excluded from metrics without identification

---

### G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Recurring revenue investment excluded from all metrics:** The filing quietly excludes one unnamed borrower from leverage, coverage, LTV, and EBITDA metrics because it is underwritten on a revenue multiple. This is a red flag: revenue-based lending in private credit has drawn scrutiny as a vector for obscuring true credit risk, particularly in software/SaaS borrowers. This borrower is invisible to investors reading headline portfolio metrics.
- **$470M unfunded commitment overhang vs. $5.7M equity raise:** The fund has nearly one-third of its committed capital still undrawn, but raised only $5.7M in new equity in June. If deployment accelerates while fundraising stalls, leverage at the fund level could increase materially.
- **Software + IT Services = ~16.5% combined concentration:** At a time when software borrower underwriting quality is under scrutiny across the private credit market, this concentration is above the level that would be considered immaterial.
- **ICAT Intermediate Holdings and Ambient Enterprises show $0 par drawn:** Two May commitments are fully undrawn. This is routine for revolvers or delayed-draw facilities, but with no sector or structure disclosed, the nature of these exposures is opaque.
- **Interest coverage of 2.4x is at the lower bound** for a healthy private-credit portfolio — any meaningful EBITDA softening in the Aerospace, IT Services, or Software cohorts could push a cluster of borrowers toward covenant pressure or payment stress.

---

### H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / expected:**
- Monthly 8-K with NAV, distribution, and portfolio snapshot — standard for non-traded private credit funds
- 95%+ senior secured portfolio composition — consistent with fund mandate
- 100% floating rate — standard for direct lending BDC-like structures
- Regulation D / Section 4(a)(2) share issuance to accredited investors — expected fundraising mechanic

# SEC Filing Analysis: Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund — 8-K / June 25, 2026

---

## A. Relevance Verdict

**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a registered private credit fund filing directly about its leverage facility — a $100M facility upsizing and a custodian transition, both executed simultaneously via a single omnibus amendment.

---

## B. One-Line Takeaway

Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund expanded its Bank of America–administered revolving credit facility by $100M to $550M while swapping out State Street as collateral custodian for Computershare, with the 60-day resignation notice requirement waived by all parties.

---

## C. What's New

- **Facility upsizing disclosed:** Maximum committed amount increased from **$450,000,000 to $550,000,000** — a $100M (22%) increase — effective June 23, 2026.
- **Collateral custodian replaced:** State Street Bank and Trust Company resigned and was replaced by **Computershare Trust Company, N.A.** as both collateral custodian and securities intermediary under the Credit Agreement and the Securities Account Control Agreement.
- **60-day notice requirement waived:** All parties — Borrower, Administrative Agent, Lenders, and Servicer — waived the contractually required 60-day prior written notice for State Street's resignation, indicating an expedited transition.
- **Omnibus Amendment executed June 23, 2026:** A single amendment modifies the Credit Agreement, the Account Control Agreement, and all related Loan Documents simultaneously to effect the custodian swap and upsizing.
- **Name change on record:** The fund was formerly named **Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund 1, LP** prior to January 2024 — this filing is under its current entity name.
- **Borrower entity confirmed:** The credit facility borrower is **Lord Abbett PCF Financing LLC**, a wholly-owned special-purpose financing subsidiary — standard NAV/warehouse leverage structure for a private credit fund.

---

## D. Most Important Points

- **Facility size: $550,000,000** (up from $450,000,000); revolving credit structure; Credit Agreement originally dated **January 23, 2025**.
- **Administrative Agent: Bank of America, N.A.** — a major bank acting as agent on a private credit fund's leverage line; consistent with banks expanding infrastructure roles in private credit.
- **Outgoing custodian: State Street Bank and Trust Company.** Resigned from both collateral custodian and securities intermediary roles simultaneously.
- **Incoming custodian: Computershare Trust Company, N.A.** Appointed immediately as successor collateral custodian and successor securities intermediary effective June 23, 2026.
- **Notice waiver:** The contractual 60-day prior notice window for custodian resignation was waived by all parties — an atypical procedural shortcut that suggests either urgency or a pre-negotiated transition timetable.
- **Structure:** Lord Abbett PCF Financing LLC (SPV/subsidiary) is the legal borrower; Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund itself serves as **servicer** — a standard two-tier leverage structure common among private credit BDCs and interval funds.
- **Registrant file number: 814-01764** — registered as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, not a standard operating company.
- **Signing officer: Salvatore Dona, CFO** of Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund.
- **Legal document reference embedded (Dechert LLP):** Document metadata references Dechert as likely counsel (NA_DECHERT.95838950.5), suggesting sophisticated fund-finance legal infrastructure.
- **Interest rate terms, maturity date, and individual lender identities:** Not disclosed in this 8-K excerpt; would be in the full Credit Agreement or prior filings.

---

## E. Why It Matters Now

The $100M facility upsizing signals that Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund is actively deploying or positioning to deploy additional leveraged capital into private credit assets — consistent with the broader theme of private credit managers expanding their capacity even as market conditions remain mixed. The custodian swap from State Street to Computershare is operationally notable: State Street has faced competitive pressure in fund-services businesses, and this may be part of a broader client migration. The waived 60-day notice requirement is the most procedurally unusual element and could suggest either a pre-agreed transition or that the parties needed to move faster than the contract allowed. There are **no visible signals of distress, non-accruals, redemption pressure, or covenant stress** in this filing — the dominant signal is fund expansion, not fund trouble.

---

---

## G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Waiver of 60-day contractual notice:** All parties, including the lenders, waived the standard resignation notice period for State Street. This is procedurally unusual and worth understanding — was this pre-planned, or was there pressure to move quickly?
- **State Street exit from a private credit custodian role:** State Street's resignation as collateral custodian and securities intermediary in a $550M private credit facility may be part of a broader pattern of State Street losing or stepping back from fund-administration mandates. Reporters covering fund services should note this.
- **$100M upsizing in the same amendment:** The facility increase was bundled with the custodian transition — it is worth asking whether the upsizing was contingent on or enabled by Computershare's willingness to take on the larger collateral set.
- **Bank of America as administrative agent:** BofA's continued role as agent on a private credit fund leverage facility is consistent with major banks deepening their private credit infrastructure relationships — worth tracking for competitive dynamics vs. Goldman, JPMorgan, Wells Fargo in this space.
- **SPV structure (Lord Abbett PCF Financing LLC):** The borrower is a special-purpose financing subsidiary — standard for private credit fund leverage, but the collateral pool composition and advance rates against it are not disclosed here; those would reveal the true risk profile of this facility.

---

## H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / Expected:**
- Use of a wholly-owned SPV as the facility borrower with the fund as servicer — standard private credit leverage structure.
- Bank of America as administrative agent on a fund-level revolving credit facility.
- Omnibus amendment format to update all loan documents simultaneously.
- 8-K filing under Items 1.01 and 2.03 for a material credit agreement amendment.
- Computershare serving as successor custodian — Computershare is an established corporate trust and custody provider.

**Potentially Non-Routine / Notable:**
- **Waiver of 60-day notice requirement** for State Street's resignation — contractual shortcut that deserves explanation.
- **Simultaneous custodian swap and facility upsizing** in one amendment — unusual bundling that may have a strategic rationale not disclosed.
- **State Street actively resigning** from a live $550M private credit facility custodian role — not a routine custodian replacement triggered by the borrower.
- **22% facility increase** (from $450M to $550M) less than 18 months after the original Credit Agreement was signed in January 2025 — rapid capacity expansion for a fund that was still relatively new.

---

## I. Questions for Follow-Up

1. **Why did State Street resign?** Was this a voluntary commercial decision, a client-initiated transition, or related to broader State Street fund-services business changes? Has State Street resigned from other private credit fund custodian roles recently?
2. **Why was the 60-day notice waiver necessary?** Did the parties need to move faster than the contract allowed? What was the operational driver for urgency?
3. **Was the $100M upsizing tied to Computershare's appointment?** Did Computershare require amended collateral terms, or did the lenders condition the upsizing on the custodian change?
4. **Who are the lenders?** The filing names Bank of America as agent but does not identify individual lenders. Is this a bank-led syndicated facility, a private credit–to–private credit leverage line, or a mix?
5. **What is the current drawn amount and advance rate?** The $550M is the committed maximum — how much is actually drawn, and what collateral is pledged against it?
6. **What is the maturity date of the Credit Agreement?** Given that the original agreement was signed January 23, 2025, a maturity date of 2–3 years out would be approaching in 2027–2028 — relevant for refinancing risk tracking.
7. **How large is the fund's total AUM relative to this $550M facility?** The leverage ratio determines how material this facility is to the fund's overall risk profile.
8. **Has Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund disclosed any non-accruals, PIK conversions, or valuation markdowns in recent filings?** The facility expansion is bullish, but portfolio credit quality is the key underlying question.

---

| 60-day notice waiver | Omnibus Amendment, Section 2.4(a) / Exhibit 10.1 | All parties waived prior notice requirement for State Street's resignation; effective immediately |
| SPV borrower structure | Item 1.01 / 8-K body | Lord Abbett PCF Financing LLC identified as "wholly-owned, special purpose financing subsidiary" |
| Original agreement date | Exhibit 10.1 recitals | Credit Agreement dated January 23, 2025 |
| Revolving facility type | Exhibit 10.1 recitals | "revolving credit facility by the Lenders for the Borrower" |
| Fund as servicer | Exhibit 10.1 parties clause | Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund named as "Servicer" — separate legal role from Borrower |
| State Street resignation basis | Exhibit 10.1, Section 2.4(a) | Resignation pursuant to Section 12.13 of Credit Agreement and Section 4(i) of Account Control Agreement |
| Prior fund name | EDGAR header | Formerly "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund 1, LP"; name changed January 2024 |

---

## K. Final Newsroom Brief

**Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund** filed an 8-K on June 25, 2026 disclosing a June 23 omnibus amendment to its revolving credit facility that does two things at once: it **replaces State Street Bank and Trust Company with Computershare Trust Company, N.A.** as collateral custodian and securities intermediary, and it **increases the facility's maximum committed amount by $100M — from $450M to $550M** — less than 18 months after the facility was originally established. The most notable procedural element is that **all parties waived the contractually required 60-day notice** for State Street's resignation, suggesting an expedited transition for reasons not explained in the filing. Bank of America, N.A. remains administrative agent. There is **no visible distress signal** in this filing — the dominant read is capacity expansion consistent with a fund actively deploying private credit capital — but reporters should press on why State Street exited, whether this custodian shift is part of a broader trend, and who the unnamed lenders are behind BofA's agent role. The facility's collateral pool composition, advance rates, drawn amount, and maturity date remain undisclosed and are the key unknowns for assessing the fund's true leverage and refinancing risk.

## SEC Filing Analysis: BlackRock Private Credit Fund (BDEBT) — 8-K / June 25, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict

**RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a routine operational 8-K for a publicly registered, non-traded private credit BDC. While the individual filing is largely procedural, the data points disclosed — subscription volume, NAV, and distributions — are directly relevant to monitoring the health and fundraising trajectory of a major retail-channel private credit fund.

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway

BlackRock Private Credit Fund (BDEBT) reports a sharply lower June share subscription of ~$4.35M, continuing a steep three-month deceleration from $21.1M in April, while NAV holds steady at $23.65 and a $0.1784 gross monthly distribution is declared.

---

### C. What's New

- **New subscription issuance disclosed:** 183,697.592 Institutional Class Shares sold to feeder vehicles on June 1, 2026 (finalized June 22, 2026) for **$4,345,329.81** — the lowest monthly subscription amount visible in recent filings.
- **New distribution declared:** $0.1784 gross per share across all share classes, declared June 23, 2026, payable July 29, 2026 to shareholders of record June 29, 2026. Net distributions vary by class after servicing fees.
- **New NAV disclosed:** $23.65 per share across all three classes (Institutional, Class S, Class D) as of May 31, 2026 — flat versus prior disclosures, signaling no material valuation event in the period.
- **Declining subscription trend newly visible:** Cross-referencing prior 8-Ks reveals a steep step-down — April finalization: 896,142.303 shares for $21.1M; May finalization: 376,795.09 shares for $8.91M; June: 183,697.592 shares for $4.35M — an ~79% decline in gross subscription proceeds over three months.
- **Tender offer activity noted in parallel filings:** A recent prior 8-K noted the Fund expects to report final results of its tender offer following the final calculation and payment of the purchase price to shareholders whose shares have been repurchased — a concurrent redemption event not disclosed in this filing but relevant context.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- **Subscription volume collapsed:** Gross feeder-vehicle subscriptions dropped from $21.1M (April) → $8.91M (May) → $4.35M (June) — a three-month decline of ~79%. This is the single most important data point in this filing series.
- **NAV stable at $23.65:** All three share classes (Institutional, S, D) carry identical NAV as of May 31, 2026. No markdown is disclosed.
- **Annualized gross yield: ~9.05%** — $0.1784 monthly distribution on $23.65 NAV = 0.754%/month × 12 = ~9.05% gross. This is within range for private credit funds but warrants monitoring if NAV or non-accruals shift.
- **Class-level net distribution spread:** Institutional: $0.1784 net; Class D: $0.1735 (after $0.0049 fee); Class S: $0.1616 (after $0.0168 fee). Class S investors bear significantly higher drag (~9.4% of gross distribution).
- **Feeder-vehicle-only Institutional issuance:** Shares are sold exclusively to feeder vehicles under Section 4(a)(2)/Regulation S exemptions — not direct retail. Institutional capital inflow is the relevant channel to track.
- **Fund is classified as an emerging growth company**, operating under SEC file number 814-01485 (Investment Company Act). The Fund offers to repurchase shares through written tender offers on a quarterly basis of up to 5% of shares outstanding, subject to Board discretion.
- **YTD return context:** As of April 30, 2026, YTD total return for the Fund was 2.02%. This is modest and below many competing interval funds for the same period.
- **No lenders, borrowers, or portfolio-level disclosures** are made in this 8-K. Underlying credit exposure must be tracked via Form N-2/A and quarterly 10-Q filings.
- **Adviser is BlackRock Capital Investment Advisors, LLC**, headquartered at 50 Hudson Yards, New York, with John M. Perlowski named in registration filings.
- A January 2026 analyst noted that BlackRock Private Credit Fund was not expected to be affected by the same NAV issues as BlackRock TCP Capital, since it does not have exposure to the same loans that caused most of the TCP NAV decline.

---

### E. Why It Matters Now

The filing itself is operationally routine, but the context is not. An analyst warned in January 2026 that negative headlines around a large traded BDC can influence investor psychology, potentially impacting fundraising momentum and increasing redemption sensitivity across parts of the private credit BDC landscape. The three-month subscription deceleration at BDEBT — from $21.1M to $4.35M — is precisely the fundraising weakness signal that analysts flagged as a secondary risk. Whether the decline reflects seasonal softness, broader NAV BDC sentiment contagion from BlackRock TCP Capital's difficulties, or the parallel impact of redemption requests draining net inflows is not determinable from this filing alone. The concurrent tender offer activity (visible in a prior 8-K) suggests outflows are occurring simultaneously with slowing inflows. This is the exact dynamic — slowing subscriptions running alongside redemption tender offers — that defines liquidity stress risk for interval/tender-offer BDC structures. No credit deterioration is disclosed, but fundraising weakness is a legitimate current concern.

---

### G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Subscription deceleration is severe and sequential:** Three straight monthly step-downs ($21.1M → $8.91M → $4.35M) warrant direct inquiry to BlackRock IR. This is not noise — it is a 79% decline in three months.
- **Concurrent tender offer unresolved:** A prior 8-K (accession 0001140361-26-025004) disclosed a pending tender offer with results not yet final. If redemption demand exceeded available liquidity or the 5% cap, that would be highly newsworthy.
- **NAV flat despite macro volatility:** The $23.65 NAV across all classes may reflect genuine portfolio stability or delayed mark-to-market. Reporters should cross-check against the most recent 10-Q for non-accruals, PIK positions, and fair-value Level 3 disclosures.
- **Low YTD return (2.02% through April):** The Fund's YTD total return as of April 30, 2026 was 2.02% — below what investors in higher-yielding private credit vehicles would expect through Q1. This could pressure net subscriptions.
- **Feeder-vehicle channel only:** All Institutional share sales go through feeder vehicles. A drop in feeder vehicle activity could signal that institutional allocators, not just retail, are pulling back — a more serious signal than retail redemption alone.

---

### H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / expected:**
- Monthly 8-K disclosure of share issuance under Item 3.02 (standard for interval/non-traded BDC structures)
- Monthly distribution declaration under Item 8.01
- Monthly NAV disclosure per share class
- Section 4(a)(2)/Regulation S exemption for feeder-vehicle share sales
- Identical NAV across all share classes (standard for this fund's pricing methodology)

**Potentially non-routine / notable:**
- **Subscription volume at a three-month low:** $4.35M is materially lower than recent monthly figures and could indicate fundraising headwinds
- **Parallel tender offer activity:** A recent prior 8-K flagged an unresolved tender offer; simultaneous low inflows and pending outflows is a structurally concerning combination for liquidity management
- **YTD return of only 2.02% through April** — underperformance relative to the fund's gross yield implies either fee drag, expense loads, or mild portfolio headwinds not fully visible in this filing
- **No Class I/S/D NAV divergence:** Uniform $23.65 NAV across all classes warrants verification — if Level 3 marks are stale, the true NAV could differ

---

### I. Questions for Follow-Up

1. **What was the final outcome of the most recent quarterly tender offer?** Did repurchase requests exceed the 5% cap, triggering proration? If so, this is a direct liquidity-management signal.
2. **What explains the sharp subscription decline from $21.1M (April) to $4.35M (June)?** Is this seasonal, distributor-driven, or a response to negative headlines around BlackRock TCP Capital?
3. **What is the fund's current net asset value on a gross vs. net basis, including any non-accruals?** The 10-Q will show this — are any portfolio companies on non-accrual or marked below cost?
4. **How does BDEBT's 2.02% YTD return compare to peer interval funds (e.g., BCRED, KCREDIT, PIMCO Private Credit)?** Underperformance could be driving the subscription drop.
5. **Who are the feeder vehicle investors behind these Institutional Class subscriptions?** Are these primarily wealth-management platforms, insurance capital, or pension allocators? A platform exit would explain the stepdown.
6. **Has the distribution coverage ratio changed?** At $0.1784/month, what is the net investment income per share for the same period? Any shortfall would imply return-of-capital risk.
7. **Is BlackRock planning any change to the quarterly tender offer size or frequency?** Given simultaneous low subscriptions and an active tender offer, a cap or gate on repurchases would be immediately newsworthy.

---

### J. Evidence from the Filing

| Item 3.02 | Shares sold to "feeder vehicles primarily created to hold the Fund's Institutional Class Shares" — exempt under Section 4(a)(2) and/or Regulation S |
| Item 8.01 — Distribution | Gross distribution: $0.1784/share; Class S net: $0.1616 (after $0.0168 fee); Class D net: $0.1735 (after $0.0049 fee); declared June 23, 2026 |
| Item 8.01 — NAV | $23.65/share, all classes, as of May 31, 2026 |
| Header | Period of report: June 22, 2026; Filed: June 25, 2026; Signatory: Erik L. Cuellar, CFO and Treasurer |
| Prior 8-K (accession 0001140361-26-025004) | Tender offer result pending: "The Fund expects to report the final results of its tender offer following the final calculation and payment" |
| Prior 8-Ks (cross-reference) | April subscription: ~$21.1M; May subscription: ~$8.91M; June: $4.35M — sequential three-month deceleration |

---

### K. Final Newsroom Brief

**INTERNAL ALERT — BlackRock Private Credit Fund (BDEBT) — 8-K, June 25, 2026**

BlackRock Private Credit Fund filed a routine 8-K disclosing a monthly share issuance of 183,697 Institutional Class shares for **$4.35M**, a declared gross distribution of **$0.1784/share**, and a stable NAV of **$23.65** across all share classes as of May 31, 2026. What is new and notable is not the individual filing but the **trend it reveals**: cross-referencing recent 8-Ks shows gross subscriptions have dropped ~79% over three months ($21.1M in April → $8.91M in May → $4.35M in June), a sharp deceleration that fits the current private-credit theme of fundraising weakness at retail-channel BDC and interval fund vehicles. The filing lands alongside an unresolved quarterly tender offer (disclosed in a prior 8-K), meaning the fund may simultaneously be processing redemption requests while new inflows dry up — a liquidity squeeze pattern worth watching closely. NAV stability and a maintained distribution rate provide no immediate crisis signal, but the subscription trend, the modest 2.02% YTD return, and analyst warnings about redemption sensitivity at BlackRock's non-traded credit franchise all warrant a follow-up inquiry to BlackRock IR before this becomes a larger story. **Priority: Watchlist / Same Day for tender offer outcome.**

**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This filing directly documents a severely oversubscribed quarterly tender in one of the largest non-traded BDCs in the market, providing hard preliminary redemption data at the epicenter of the current private-credit liquidity stress theme.

### B. One-Line Takeaway

ASIF's Q2 2026 tender was nearly 3x oversubscribed — with 14.4% of shares tendered against a 5% cap — confirming that redemption pressure is intensifying quarter-over-quarter at a $22.6 billion private-credit fund.

### C. What's New

- **Preliminary proration rate disclosed for first time:** The fund prorated Q1 2026 redemption requests, accepting 43.1% of tendered shares. The Q2 2026 proration worsens materially to **34.7%** of requested amounts — meaning only one-in-three redemption dollars gets out the door this quarter.
- **Oversubscription magnitude now quantified:** The filing discloses for the first time that **56,891,917 shares**, representing **14.4% of shares outstanding as of April 30, 2026**, were tendered before the June 18, 2026 expiration — against a hard 5% cap.
- **Tender expiration confirmed:** The offer closed at 4:00 p.m. ET on June 18, 2026, with the valuation date set at May 31, 2026.
- **New shareholder-facing materials added:** Amendment No. 1 introduces a "Q2 Tender Offer Update" (Exhibit a(1)(vi)) and a "Tender Offer Frequently Asked Questions" (Exhibit a(1)(vii)) — suggestive of escalating investor communication needs.

- **No carryover of unfulfilled requests:** The filing reconfirms that unmet redemptions do **not** roll over to the next quarter; investors must resubmit — a structural liquidity friction disclosed anew to current shareholders who are partially frozen out.
- **New market signal embedded in marketing exhibit:** The Q2 Update discloses that new deal activity is accelerating "at wider spreads, higher upfront fees and more lender-friendly terms" — a forward-looking signal on private-credit market conditions not in the original May 20 filing.

### D. Most Important Points

- **14.4% tendered vs. 5% cap:** Oversubscription ratio of ~2.88x means ASIF is absorbing far more exit pressure than its liquidity framework was designed to handle on a single-quarter basis.
- **Proration worsened quarter-over-quarter:** Q1 2026 filled 43.1% of requests; Q2 fills only 34.7% — a deterioration of ~840 basis points in the fill rate, suggesting demand to exit is outpacing any investor-base stabilization.
- Q1 2026: investors submitted more than $1.2 billion in redemption requests against a 5% quarterly cap, with the fund paying out $523.5 million. Q2 appears larger in relative terms.
- **Fund size: $22.6 billion total assets** across 831 portfolio companies, average position size 0.1% — well-diversified but size doesn't insulate from the liquidity mismatch.

## SEC Filing Analysis: Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S — SC TO-I/A (Final Amendment), June 9, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict

**RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a direct private credit fund liquidity-management filing. The zero-tender result is the operative data point: it is either a benign sign that investors are not seeking exits, or a structural signal about the fund's early-stage or nascent investor base.

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway

Lord Abbett's private credit fund ran a formal tender offer for up to 316,839.86 shares and attracted **zero** tenders — a notable null result that inverts the typical redemption-pressure story dominating private credit headlines.

---

### C. What's New

- **Zero tenders received.** The final amendment confirms that no shares were validly tendered before the May 29, 2026 expiration. The fund will purchase no shares. This is the operative new disclosure — the offer resulted in null participation.
- **Tender offer cycle completed.** The offer was originally filed April 30, 2026, and expired May 29, 2026 — a roughly 30-day window. This amendment closes the cycle.
- **NAV-based pricing with future valuation date.** The purchase price was to equal NAV *as of June 30, 2026* — a date approximately one month after the offer expiration, meaning investors would have tendered blind to the final price.
- **Entity previously named "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund A, LP."** The fund formally changed its name to "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S" in October 2024, signaling a structural conversion from LP partnership form to a fund/trust structure with common shares of beneficial interest (par value $0.01).
- **This is at least the second tender offer cycle.** A prior SC TO-I filing from August 2025 referenced a similar issuer tender offer, indicating the fund runs periodic liquidity windows — consistent with a non-traded BDC or registered private credit fund structure.
- **No CUSIP assigned.** Shares have no CUSIP number, confirming no secondary market exists and consistent with a non-traded fund structure.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- **Zero shares tendered out of up to 316,839.86 offered for repurchase.** The fund was prepared to repurchase a defined number of shares; no investor exercised the window.
- **Original tender offer dated April 30, 2026; expired May 29, 2026.** The window was approximately 29 days.
- **Purchase price tied to NAV as of June 30, 2026** — a future date roughly 32 days after the offer expiration, creating a price-at-time-of-tender uncertainty for shareholders.
- **Filer/Issuer is Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund S**, managed by **Lord Abbett Private Credit Advisor LLC**, located at 30 Hudson Street, Jersey City, NJ — part of Lord Abbett & Co. LLC's broader private credit platform.

- **Delaware-incorporated; common shares of beneficial interest** — structure is consistent with a non-traded BDC, registered closed-end fund, or similar private credit vehicle, not a typical LP/hedge fund.
- **Entity previously operated as "Lord Abbett Private Credit Fund A, LP"** — the conversion away from LP structure, dated October 2024, suggests an organizational build-out or restructuring that preceded this tender offer program.
- The fund appears to target accredited investors only, consistent with a private placement or limited distribution channel.
- There is no secondary market for the fund's shares, and none is expected to develop, making tender offers the sole exit mechanism for shareholders.

### E. Why It Matters Now

The dominant private credit narrative in mid-2026 is **investor redemption pressure** — gates, tender limits, and oversubscribed repurchase windows at non-traded BDCs and interval funds. This filing runs directly counter to that: a private credit fund opened a formal buyback window and received **zero** investor requests to exit. That outcome is ambiguous. It could mean the fund is early-stage, thinly populated, or has a locked-up investor base that did not engage with the window; it could also mean investors genuinely have no exit motivation. There is no secondary market for shares, and there is no guarantee that an investor will be able to tender all or any of their requested shares in a periodic repurchase offer — but here, the inverse occurred: zero demand to use the available liquidity. ## SEC Filing Analysis: TPG Twin Brook Capital Income Fund (TCAP) — 8-K / June 8, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict

**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

This is a non-traded BDC filing a proactive Reg FD business update at precisely the moment that non-traded BDC redemption pressure is the most-watched story in private credit. The filing is explicitly designed to counter that narrative.

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway

As BofA analysts warned that non-traded BDC redemption requests would peak in Q2 2026 with most funds proration requests exceeding 5% limits, TCAP is publicly flagging that its own redemption requests are only 2.1% of shares outstanding and will be honored in full — a direct contrast to severely stressed peers.

---

### C. What's New

- **Q2 2026 repurchase rate disclosed mid-quarter:** TCAP reports that repurchase requests stand at **2.1% of shares outstanding** as of March 31, 2026 (~$53 million based on March 31 NAV) — the fund explicitly states it will honor all requests, well below the 5% quarterly program limit. This is a proactive, mid-quarter disclosure, not a routine quarterly report.

- **New inflow figure (April 1 – June 8, 2026):** Capital inflows of approximately **$181 million** are reported for the period April 1 through June 8, 2026, excluding June dividend reinvestments — a freshly minted number not in any prior quarterly filing.

- **Explicit software exposure quantification:** The filing discloses **~2% of fair value** in software exposure. This is a direct response to a known industry concern and represents a newly flagged portfolio-composition figure in an investor-facing document.

- **Liquidity position confirmed at $832 million as of March 31, 2026:** Disclosed via this Reg FD update; not previously disclosed in this format or period.

- **Q1 2026 new subscriptions figure:** $193 million of new subscriptions received during Q1 2026 — a current-quarter fundraising data point newly disclosed outside of the formal quarterly report cycle.

- **Fund name change history now disclosed in filing header:** The filing header confirms the fund was formerly named "AG Twin Brook Capital Income Fund" before renaming to "TPG Twin Brook Capital Income Fund" — relevant for reporters tracking the TPG Angelo Gordon rebrand.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- Industry-wide, non-traded BDCs are designed with 5% quarterly redemption limits, and BofA analysts warned in April that advisors were requesting more than needed in reaction to prorations. TCAP's 2.1% request rate positions it as a clear outlier relative to the most stressed peers.

- Apollo Debt Solutions saw Q1 redemption requests of 11.2% and BCRED hit 7.9% — making TCAP's 2.1% and full-honor commitment a material competitive differentiator that reporters should verify against actual peer data.

- Portfolio size is **$4.5 billion across 270 positions**, with an average position size of **0.37%** of fair value — granular diversification claim that reduces single-name concentration risk.

- PIK interest rate is **1.3%** and non-accrual rate is **0.2%** on an amortized cost basis (0.1% fair value), with "minimal to no change from the prior quarter." These are notably low by BDC standards at this stage of the cycle.

- Interest coverage ratio is **2.4x** — calculated using LTM EBITDA vs. cash interest at average 3-month SOFR. Disclosed with a caveat that financials are 90 days in arrears and not independently verified.

- Loan-to-value at closing: **40%** weighted average across first lien term loans, funded DDTLs, and revolvers — a structurally conservative underwriting figure.

- **Debt-to-equity ratio of 0.8x** (from a prior filing) — below average for non-traded BDC peers, consistent with Fitch's observation that non-traded BDCs averaged 0.71x leverage vs. 1.13x for listed BDCs.

- Average portfolio company EBITDA at origination: **$18.3 million** — lower middle market focus, distinct from large-cap or upper-middle-market private credit platforms.

- Annualized distribution rate: **9.9%**, with a footnote warning that distributions may be funded from sources other than operating cash flow, including borrowings or return of capital.

- Selectivity: **<4% of transactions screened** are closed, a figure that applies to the broader TPG Twin Brook platform since 2014 — not just TCAP.

---

### E. Why It Matters Now

Moody's noted that inflows for perpetually non-traded BDCs shifted to a first-ever net outflow in Q1 2026. Blue Owl saw a surge in redemption requests in late February 2026 and effectively "gated" certain retail-focused vehicles. TCAP's June 8 Reg FD filing is a deliberate, mid-quarter preemptive communication designed to separate the fund from the distress narrative dominating non-traded BDC coverage. The 2.1% redemption rate and explicit "all requests will be honored" statement are its core counterarguments. Reporters should treat this as a marketing document — factually specific but clearly motivated by a need to reassure investors and distribution channel partners during a period of sector-wide anxiety. The filing does not disclose any new credit stress, troubled borrowers, or covenant amendments; the private-credit relevance here is entirely through the redemption-liquidity lens.

---

### F. Filing Details Extracted

### G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Redemption rate is suspiciously low vs. the industry:** Blue Owl's OCIC saw 21.9% withdrawal requests and OTIC saw 40.7% in Q1, making TCAP's 2.1% claim worth independently verifying through transfer agent data or rival fund disclosures.

- **Mid-quarter Reg FD filing is uncommon and tactical:** Filing a business update 8-K in June — between quarterly earnings filings — signals that management is actively managing the redemption narrative. That itself is newsworthy.

- **Software exposure explicitly called out at ~2%:** A prior TCAP 8-K from March 2026 acknowledged "concerns regarding the potential for AI-disruption in the software sector, increased asset class redemptions, and credit quality" — the June filing's explicit ~2% software figure is a direct response to that specific investor concern.

- **Distribution sustainability footnote:** The filing warns that distributions may be funded from "borrowings, return of capital or offering proceeds" — a standard BDC disclosure but one reporters should flag given sector-wide pressure on distribution coverage.

- **$181M of inflows April–June 2026 during a net-outflow quarter for the industry:** If accurate, this is a significant counter-trend claim. Reporters should ask whether this figure is gross inflows or net of redemptions, and what the transfer agent's methodology is.

---

### H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / Expected:**
- 100% first lien senior secured portfolio composition disclosure
- EBITDA-based interest coverage disclosure (2.4x) with standard 90-day lag caveat
- Standard BDC risk disclosures (past performance, non-GAAP, distribution sources)
- Outperformance vs. leveraged loan and fixed income benchmarks marketing language
- Footnotes on non-accrual methodology, PIK calculation, and LTV weighting

**Potentially Non-Routine / Notable:**
- Mid-quarter Reg FD 8-K filed during the peak of BDC redemption stress — timing is deliberate and editorial
- Explicit statement: "TCAP will honor **all** repurchase requests this quarter" — most stressed BDCs cannot say this
- Freshly reported inflow figure ($181M, April–June 2026) predates the formal quarterly report, suggesting management wants this number in the market now
- Explicit 2% software cap disclosure — targeted response to a specific industry concern
- Repurchase requests described as "approximately 2% or less and 100% fulfilled **since inception**" — a structural historical claim that warrants scrutiny as industry conditions worsen

---

### I. Questions for Follow-Up

1. **Is the $181M inflow figure gross or net of redemptions?** The filing says "not including June dividend reinvestments" but does not net against repurchase requests — this matters significantly for the fundraising story.

2. **Why file a Reg FD 8-K now, mid-quarter?** What triggered management's decision to disclose proactively in early June rather than wait for Q2 earnings? Was there distributor or investor-channel pressure?

3. **How does TCAP's 2.1% redemption rate compare to the broader TPG wealth platform?** Are any other TPG-affiliated vehicles showing higher redemption rates that could create cross-product pressure?

4. **What is the actual composition of the $832M liquidity figure?** How much is undrawn revolving credit vs. cash? What are the borrowing base constraints on those revolvers?

5. **The interest coverage ratio is 2.4x — how has this trended quarter-over-quarter?** The filing says "minimal to no change" on PIK and non-accrual, but does not disclose prior-period coverage, which matters for trend analysis.

6. **Are any of the 270 portfolio companies experiencing covenant pressure or maturity wall stress?** The filing is silent on amendments, waivers, or maturity extensions, which does not mean they don't exist.

7. **Who are the revolving credit facility lenders providing the majority of the $832M liquidity?** Identifying whether these are bank lines or private credit facilities matters for structural resilience.

8. **Has TCAP itself extended or amended any portfolio company loan terms in Q1–Q2 2026?** The low non-accrual rate is reassuring, but forbearance or maturity extensions would not necessarily appear in this metric.

---

### J. Evidence from the Filing

*(All from Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure — Business Update section)*

- **On redemptions:** The filing states repurchase requests represent **2.1% of shares outstanding** as of March 31, 2026, or ~$53 million based on March 31 NAV — "below our program's 5% quarterly repurchase limit" — and that TCAP "will honor all repurchase requests this quarter."

- **On inflows:** Capital inflows from April 1 through June 8, 2026 were "approximately $181 million, not including June dividend reinvestments."

- **On non-accruals and PIK:** PIK at 1.3% of total investment income (three months ended March 31, 2026); non-accrual rate at 0.2% amortized cost / 0.1% fair value, "with minimal to no change from the prior quarter."

- **On software risk:** Fund has "limited software exposure of approximately 2% of fair value."

- **On liquidity:** "Over $832 million of available liquidity as of March 31, 2026" composed of cash plus undrawn revolving credit facility capacity.

- **On distribution sustainability (footnote 3):** Explicitly discloses TCAP "may fund distributions from sources other than cash flow from operations, including, without limitation, the sale of assets, borrowings, return of capital or offering proceeds."

- **On underwriting selectivity:** References closing "less than 4% of transactions screened" — but this figure applies to the **TPG Twin Brook platform since 2014**, not TCAP alone since 2022.

---

### K. Final Newsroom Brief

**INTERNAL ALERT — June 8, 2026**

TPG Twin Brook Capital Income Fund (TCAP), a $4.5 billion non-traded BDC managed by TPG Angelo Gordon, filed an unusual mid-quarter Reg FD 8-K on June 8, 2026, disclosing that Q2 2026 repurchase requests total only 2.1% of shares outstanding (~$53M), well below its 5% quarterly cap, and that all requests will be honored in full. The fund simultaneously disclosed $181 million in new capital inflows between April 1 and June 8, 2026, and $832 million in available liquidity — figures that stand in sharp contrast to peers facing redemption gates. HPS' HLEND was forecast to see 13% redemption requests in Q2, and Blue Owl's OTIC was projected at 52.9%, making TCAP's disclosure a deliberate competitive positioning move. The filing is non-routine in timing and intent — management clearly wants these numbers in the market ahead of formal Q2 earnings — and reporters should probe whether the $181M inflow figure is gross or net of redemptions, and whether any portfolio-level stress (covenant waivers, maturity extensions) exists beneath the headline metrics. Nothing in the filing signals credit deterioration, but the absence of any portfolio-level detail on amendments or troubled credits leaves material questions unanswered.

## SEC Filing Analysis: Blackstone Private Credit Fund (BCRED) — SC TO-I/A, June 4, 2026

---

### A. Relevance Verdict
**HIGHLY RELEVANT TO PRIVATE CREDIT**

---

### B. One-Line Takeaway
BCRED's Q2 tender offer update discloses that redemption requests have surged to ~10% of shares outstanding — double the standard cap — forcing the fund to pro-rate repurchases at the 5% limit for the first time this cycle.

---

### C. What's New

- **Q2 redemption requests hit ~10% of shares outstanding** — twice the fund's standard 5% quarterly repurchase cap and materially above Q1's level (which required a Board override to 7% to clear all requests).
- **BCRED will NOT fulfill all Q2 requests**; it will honor only 5% of shares outstanding on a pro-rata basis, meaning a significant portion of tendering investors will receive less than they requested. This is a structural break from Q1 behavior.
- **Net outflow of ~3% of NAV in Q2** disclosed, with capital inflows of only ~2% of NAV — consistent with Q1's net outflow, suggesting persistent net redemption pressure is not improving.
- **Bottom 5% of the private debt portfolio is marked at 68.3** as of April 30, 2026 — a more granular distress disclosure than previously seen in BCRED communications; implies ~31.7 cents on the dollar impairment at the tail.
- **PIK income as a % of total investment income declined 11% sequentially** in Q1 vs. Q4 — newly disclosed metric, framed positively but signals PIK was a meaningful concern in prior quarters.
- **BCRED committed to a portion of a Blackstone-led $10 billion senior secured financing to Firmus Technologies**, an AI infrastructure platform — first formal confirmation of BCRED's participation in this mega-deal within a public filing.
- **Onshore repurchase volumes below prior quarter levels** in the back half of Q2's offer period — a specific new signal of demand deceleration within the current tender window.

---

### D. Most Important Points

- In Q1, Blackstone raised BCRED's quarterly repurchase limit above the standard 5% to 7%, with the firm and its employees stepping in to cover the gap, in order to meet 100% of withdrawal requests as redemption pressure rose. In Q2, that approach is no longer being applied — BCRED will pro-rate at 5%.

- The filing discloses Q2 repurchase requests are **approximately 10% of shares outstanding**. Against a 5% fulfillment cap, this means roughly half of tendering investors will be partially turned away — a meaningful investor-experience deterioration.

- BCRED faced $1.7 billion of net withdrawals in its latest fiscal quarter, the largest since its early 2021 inception, alongside gross withdrawals exceeding the 7% quarterly maximum it can legally meet without changing its tender offer.

- **Portfolio mark: 96.1** as of April 30, 2026 — broadly in line with syndicated loans, but the **bottom 5% of the private debt portfolio is marked at 68.3**, suggesting meaningful tail-risk concentration in underperforming positions.

- **Interest coverage: 2.2x** as of March 31, 2026, described as a 40% improvement over two years — a signal of portfolio health, but the absolute level remains modest for a leveraged credit portfolio.

- **Available liquidity: over $15 billion** (cash + undrawn borrowing capacity); fund leverage at **0.8x debt-to-equity** — Blackstone is heavily emphasizing balance sheet resilience to push back on redemption-pressure narrative.

- **Q1 deployment: over $4 billion**, including a commitment to a portion of a $10 billion debt financing facility led by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities, Blackstone Credit & Insurance, and affiliated funds for Australian AI infrastructure company Firmus Technologies.

- The financing is intended to fund the next phase of Project Southgate — Firmus' national rollout of its AI Factory platform, based on the NVIDIA DSX reference architecture.

- **Distribution rate: 10.0% for Class I shares**, framed as 200+ bps above leveraged loans — but the sustainability of this rate amid net outflows and tail markdowns is not explicitly addressed.

- **Since inception (2021): 9.3% annualized total return for Class I**, claimed to outperform leveraged loans by approximately 320 basis points.

---

### E. Why It Matters Now

This filing sits squarely at the intersection of two of the most-watched private credit themes right now: **redemption pressure in semi-liquid BDC/private credit funds** and **aggressive AI-infrastructure lending**. The Q2 redemption surge to ~10% — and BCRED's decision to pro-rate at 5% rather than engineer a repeat of Q1's full-clearance maneuver — is the clearest sign yet that investor withdrawal demand is outpacing Blackstone's willingness or ability to keep covering the gap. The contrast with Blue Owl Capital Corporation II is stark: following a failed merger, Blue Owl effectively converted that BDC into a drawdown vehicle after walking back its promise to resume quarterly redemptions, returning capital whether shareholders wanted it or not and at a time not of their choosing. BCRED has not gone that far, but the pro-rata gate on Q2 repurchases is a directional step toward tighter liquidity management. The bottom-5% portfolio mark of 68.3 and the prior-quarter PIK disclosure add a layer of portfolio-quality concern that the headline 96.1 average mark obscures. The Firmus AI-infrastructure commitment is separately notable as one of the largest private credit deals in Australian history — but reporters should scrutinize whether BCRED's exposure to an early-stage, formerly crypto-focused neocloud at $10 billion notional size represents an underwriting risk in a "growth-at-all-costs" AI lending cycle.

---

### F. Filing Details Extracted

| **Dollar Amounts** | Tender offer up to 93,100,275 shares; Q2 repurchase requests ~10% of shares outstanding; Q2 cap: 5% of shares; Q1 repurchase cap lifted to 7%; Q1 deployment >$4 billion; Firmus financing: $10 billion senior secured; Q1 loan repayments: $2.6 billion; Q2 inflows: ~$1 billion; Available liquidity: >$15 billion |
| **Maturity Dates** | Valuation date for Q2 tender offer: June 30, 2026 |

---

### G. Signals Reporters Should Notice

- **Redemption gate effectively triggered at 5% in Q2**: Unlike Q1, Blackstone is not engineering full clearance. Investors requesting above the 5% cap will be pro-rated. This is the first formal cap-out in BCRED's post-inception history and a structural liquidity-management action worth tracking across the BDC sector.

- **Bottom 5% of portfolio at 68.3**: The tail of BCRED's private debt book carries significant impairment. Blackstone's framing that "underperforming assets are reflected in current valuations" is carefully worded — reporters should ask which sectors or borrowers make up this cohort and whether any are software/tech.

- **Firmus Technologies exposure — AI infrastructure underwriting risk**: Firmus's revenue has not been publicly disclosed, and the $10 billion Blackstone debt facility creates substantial financial obligations that must be serviced regardless of whether demand materializes as expected. BCRED's portion of this commitment is undisclosed; asking for the specific tranche size is warranted.

- **PIK income decline framed as positive, but the baseline was elevated**: The 11% sequential decline in PIK as a share of total investment income in Q1 vs. Q4 implies PIK had been rising — a stress signal not previously foregrounded in BCRED public materials.

- **Net outflow of ~3% of NAV for second consecutive quarter**: Despite Blackstone employee co-investment in Q1 and >$15 billion in stated liquidity, outflows are not decelerating. The filing notes onshore volumes were "below prior quarter levels" in the back half of Q2 — a possible signal of accelerating retail investor fatigue.

---

### H. Routine vs. Non-Routine

**Routine / Expected:**
- Amendment filing (SC TO-I/A) to add an investor letter update — procedurally standard for quarterly tender cycles
- Restatement of fund performance, NAV metrics, and distribution rates
- Disclosure that repurchases are subject to Board approval and pro-rata allocation when requests exceed the cap — this is pre-disclosed in the prospectus
- Liquidity disclosures (cash + undrawn facilities) as part of investor reassurance messaging
- Legal counsel and transfer agent identification

**Potentially Non-Routine / Notable:**
- Q2 redemption requests reaching ~10% of shares outstanding — double the cap, and above even the Q1 level that triggered the emergency Board override
- Decision NOT to repeat the Q1 full-clearance strategy (no Board override to cover above 5% this quarter), representing a policy shift
- Granular tail-of-portfolio disclosure (bottom 5% at 68.3) — more specific stress disclosure than typical BCRED communications
- Disclosure of BCRED's direct participation in the Firmus $10 billion AI infrastructure deal — significant single-credit concentration in an unrated, early-stage Australian neocloud
- PIK income as a percentage of investment income declining 11% sequentially, implying prior quarter stress

---

### I. Questions for Follow-Up

1. **How much of BCRED's capital is committed to the Firmus $10 billion facility, and what is BCRED's specific tranche size, seniority, and collateral package?** Is this secured solely against hardware/GPU assets, real property, or contractual revenue?

2. **Which borrowers or sectors make up the bottom 5% of the portfolio marked at 68.3?** Is there software, real estate, or consumer exposure in this cohort?

3. **Why did Blackstone choose NOT to repeat the Q1 Board override strategy in Q2?** Is this a capital-preservation decision, a signal that the employee co-investment well is depleted, or a deliberate normalization of the gate?

4. **What is the dollar value of the ~10% Q2 redemption requests, and how does it compare to BCRED's total NAV?** Given the fund's earlier ~$82 billion AUM figure, even 5% represents multi-billion-dollar outflows.

5. **Is the PIK-income-as-percentage-of-income decline driven by base-rate cuts, genuine borrower improvement, or amendments that converted PIK to cash pay?** The distinction matters for credit quality assessment.

6. **How does BCRED's Q2 redemption trajectory compare to peers such as Blue Owl, Ares Capital, and FS KKR?** Is this a fund-specific dynamic or part of a broader retail private credit redemption wave?

7. **What happens to investors whose Q2 requests are pro-rated — do they automatically roll into the Q3 tender window, and is there any penalty or re-queue mechanism?**

8. Given that Firmus made a pivot from crypto mining to AI infrastructure and is still relatively early in its evolution as a data center operator, what due diligence process did Blackstone Credit use to underwrite a $10 billion facility, and who are the contracted end-customers generating the cash flows that service the debt?

---

### J. Evidence from the Filing

All citations below are from **Exhibit (a)(1)(vii) — Q2 Distribution and Tender Offer Update**, dated June 4, 2026, filed as part of the SC TO-I/A:

- **On Q2 redemption surge and cap**: *"In Q2, repurchase requests are approximately 10% of shares outstanding… BCRED will fulfill repurchase requests representing 5% of shares outstanding."* — This is the filing's single most material new disclosure. The pro-rata cap has been formally invoked.

- **On Q1 override precedent**: *"In Q1… the Board increased the repurchase cap above the 5% level to fulfill all requests at 7%."* — This confirms Q1 was exceptional; Q2 reverts to standard cap, making the pro-rata gate operative.

- **On portfolio tail**: *"The bottom 5% of the private debt portfolio [is] marked at 68.3 as of April 30, 2026."* — Compared with the headline 96.1, this implies a 31.7-point impairment in the weakest positions.

- **On PIK trend**: *"Payment-in-kind income as a percentage of total investment income declined by 11% sequentially in Q1 vs. Q4."* — Framed as a positive trend; baseline implies prior-quarter PIK elevation.

- **On Firmus deal**: *"BCRED… committed to a portion of a Blackstone-led $10 billion senior secured financing to AI infrastructure platform Firmus Technologies."* — The transaction marks one of the largest private debt financings in Australian history.

- **On net flows**: *"Capital inflows are approximately 2% of NAV, resulting in a net outflow of approximately 3% of NAV, consistent with Q1."* — Two consecutive quarters of net outflows now on record.

- **On onshore deceleration**: *"Repurchase activity decelerated in the back half of the offer period, with onshore volumes below prior quarter levels."* — Points to retail investor fatigue or advisor channel softness in the U.S.

---

### K. Final Newsroom Brief

**BCRED — Q2 2026 Tender Update: Redemption Gate Now Operative**

Blackstone Private Credit Fund (BCRED) filed an amendment to its Q2 tender offer on June 4, 2026, disclosing that investor redemption requests have surged to approximately 10% of shares outstanding — double the fund's standard 5% quarterly repurchase cap. Unlike Q1, when Blackstone's Board raised the cap to 7% and had employees co-invest to clear 100% of requests, the fund will pro-rate Q2 repurchases at 5%, meaning a substantial portion of tendering investors will not receive full proceeds this quarter. This is the first formal invocation of the pro-rata gate in BCRED's post-inception history and represents a meaningful escalation in the fund's redemption-pressure story. The filing also discloses that the bottom 5% of BCRED's private debt portfolio is marked at 68.3 — implying roughly 32 cents of impairment at the tail — alongside a newly disclosed prior-quarter PIK-income trend that suggests borrower stress was more elevated heading into 2026 than headline marks suggested. The Firmus Technologies AI infrastructure deal ($10 billion senior secured, Blackstone-led) is confirmed as an active BCRED commitment, raising questions about underwriting standards and concentration risk in an unproven, formerly crypto-focused borrower. Reporters should treat this as a priority story: the combination of a first-ever Q2 gate, persistent ~3% net quarterly outflows, a distressed portfolio tail, and a mega AI-infrastructure bet that lacks public revenue disclosure collectively signals that BCRED's private-credit-stress narrative is deepening, not stabilizing.

Interest coverage: 2.2x** as of March 31, 2026, described as a 40% improvement over two years — a signal of portfolio health, but the absolute level remains modest for a leveraged credit portfolio.

Available liquidity: over $15 billion** (cash + undrawn borrowing capacity); fund leverage at **0.8x debt-to-equity** — Blackstone is heavily emphasizing balance sheet resilience to push back on redemption-pressure narrative.

Q1 deployment: over $4 billion**, including a commitment to a portion of a $10 billion debt financing facility led by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities, Blackstone Credit & Insurance, and affiliated funds for Australian AI infrastructure company Firmus Technologies.
The financing is intended to fund the next phase of Project Southgate — Firmus' national rollout of its AI Factory platform, based on the NVIDIA DSX reference architecture.
Distribution rate: 10.0% for Class I shares**, framed as 200+ bps above leveraged loans — but the sustainability of this rate amid net outflows and tail markdowns is not explicitly addressed.
Since inception (2021): 9.3% annualized total return for Class I**, claimed to outperform leveraged loans by approximately 320 basis points.
